s: Mehr als drei Millionen Menschen wären vom sekundenschnellen Hitzetod bedroht, würde der Vesuv noch einmal so gewaltig explodieren wie im Jahr 79 nach Christus.

still, yet (up to and including a given time)
still, eventually, sometime (at an unspecified time in the future)
We may still need that sometime.
additionally, in addition, besides, else; more often expressed in English with another, more
Seins ist sehr schön, aber deins ist noch schöner!
His is very pretty, but yours is even prettier!
Oder besser noch: du machst es sofort.
Or better still: you do it right away.
Added to parting phrases that express a wish for the following period of time.
Have a nice (rest of your) evening!
Gives vague temporal nuances, e.g. that something is over, or that it follows something else.
Nach der Arbeit gehen wir oft noch was trinken.
After work we often go out for drinks.
Emphasizes that something has been preserved, inherited, passed on.
Der Ohrring ist noch von meiner Oma.
This earring was handed down from my Grandma.
Diese Straßenschilder sind noch aus der Kaiserzeit.
These street signs go all the way back to the Kaiser’s days.
noch.et: From Middle High German noch, nog, from Old High German noh, from Proto-West Germanic *noh, from Proto-Germanic *nuh, from Proto-Indo-European *nu (“now”) + *-kʷe (“and, also”). Cognate to Dutch nog and noch (which are etymologically the same word).

s: nor; function word introducing each except the first term or series, indicating none of them is true
Ich mag weder ihn noch dich.
I like neither him nor you.
Er versteht es nicht, noch wird er es jemals verstehen.
He doesn’t understand it, nor will he ever understand it.
noch.et: From Middle High German noch, nog, from Old High German noh, from Proto-West Germanic *noh, from Proto-Germanic *nuh, from Proto-Indo-European *nu (“now”) + *-kʷe (“and, also”). Cognate to Dutch nog and noch (which are etymologically the same word).
